source_anchors.purpose: Real recovery image is still required and copied before the optional non-A/B artifact.
Previously attempted non-A/B two-step construction for every new recovery image.
The pinned recovery-fstab loader already excludes the same A/B-only mode.
BOOTABLE_IMAGES returns the exact prebuilt without AVB re-signing.
Two-step recovery is written to boot, not the dedicated recovery partition.
Non-A/B on an A/B device requires explicit allow_non_ab metadata.

limitations: This is a follow-up to the reviewed prebuilt recovery consumer, not a replacement for it.
An A/B-only target has no recovery-two-step.img consumer. The preserved recovery.img belongs in its recovery payload partition.
The 100 MiB kernel-free working76 image does not fit the 96 MiB Nezha boot partition and is not a two-step boot image. No such artifact is created.
Non-A/B and hybrid A/B/non-A/B products retain upstream two-step construction and its missing-image assertion; no error is suppressed for those modes.
The unchanged pinned OTA tool rejects force_non_ab when allow_non_ab is not true. Nezha must remain A/B-only.
The first-stage recovery branch can be verified with synthetic bytes, but that is not a full target-files build, AVB validation, payload signing, OTA installation or runtime test.
A complete target-files build still requires all image inputs, mi_ext integration, signed AVB descriptors, partition-fit checks, full VINTF and labeling compatibility, and reviewed OTA trust.
Upstream target-files validators do not establish all of those properties: raw non-sparse image consistency and OTA key reconciliation require independent checks.
